## Analysis

- **Alaska posts the highest reported FY2024 growth (+12.6%)**, but stripping out the $869M of acquired Hawaiian revenue [alaska_10k_note_acquisition.txt] leaves organic growth of roughly **+4.2%** — below Delta, United and Southwest. Its growth is acquisition-driven, not momentum.
- **United is the strongest on a comparable, organic basis**: +6.23% in FY2024 (edging Delta's +6.19%) and clearly the best two-year trajectory at **+12.7% CAGR** vs. Delta's +10.4%, driven by a +19.5% FY2023 rebound.
- **Delta** is a close second — largest absolute revenue base ($61.6B) and essentially tied on FY2024 growth.
- **Southwest** (+5.3%) and especially **American** (+2.7% in FY2024, +5.2% two-year CAGR) show the weakest momentum; American decelerated the most.

Because Alaska's outperformance is inorganic and its underlying growth lags, United has the strongest genuine revenue growth momentum.

ANSWER: United Airlines — on a comparable (organic) basis it had the strongest momentum: +6.2% in FY2024 (57,063M vs 53,717M) and the best two-year CAGR at ~12.7%, just ahead of Delta (+6.2% FY24; 10.4% CAGR). Alaska's higher reported +12.6% FY2024 growth is not comparable, as it includes $869M of Hawaiian revenue post-September 18, 2024 acquisition (organic growth only ~4.2%); Southwest (+5.3%) and American (+2.7%) were weakest.
